item.title: ‘You’re going to have every college in the country go bankrupt’: Donald Trump urges passing of college sports bill before Democrats take over
item.description: President Donald J. Trump speaks during the Trump Midterm Rally at F&M Bank Arena in Clarksville, Tenn., Saturday, October. 10, 2026. President Donald Trump has made it clear for months that he wants the Protect College Sports Act signed into law. But with Democrats set to take control of Congress in January, the clock is running out on the bill. On Friday, Trump once again called on Congress to pass the bill, warning that “every college in the country” will go bankrupt if it doesn’t. The push comes as House Republicans are reportedly working on revisions that could set up a vote after Thanksgiving. Protect College Sports Act Stalled In House The Protect College Sports Act, co-sponsored by Republican Senator Ted Cruz, aims to set national rules for NIL, revenue sharing, transfers, and eligibility in college sports. The bill passed the Senate by a 77-22 vote , but it has stalled in the House. House Majority Leader Steve Scalise previously said that the bill had “ some other problems ” that needed to be fixed. Then, Democrats won control of both the House and Senate in the midterm elections, putting the bill’s future in serious doubt. Now, according to a report from Ross Dellenger of On3, the House is working on small revisions to the bill, including raising the cap on Power Four conference membership from 20 schools to 22. Scalise said that a vote on a narrowly revised version could happen after Thanksgiving. But time is short. The House returns on Nov. 30 for a final three-week session before the current Congress adjourns on Dec. 17, according to On3. If the bill doesn’t pass by then, the process will have to start over when the new Congress takes over in January. And if the House makes enough changes, the bill would also have to go back to the Senate. ‘Colleges don’t have that kind of money’ Trump brought up the bill during a press conference on Friday, while discussing legislation that he believes can get bipartisan support. And in the middle of his answer, he appeared to take a shot at Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood . “So, you’re going to have colleges, every college is going to go bankrupt if we don’t get a bill done because they’re going crazy. They’re paying quarterbacks $12 million a year. They have one guy, he’s got a strong arm, but no accuracy. Good. He’s getting $12 million. He’s 17 years old. It’s not going to work out,” Trump said, via the White House . Trump then turned his attention to the financial state of college athletic departments. “But what’s happening is they have no cap. item.title: Elliot Anderson urges calm as Manchester City stumble again in frustrating Fulham draw
item.description: Elliot Anderson urges calm as Manchester City stumble again in frustrating Fulham draw Elliot Anderson has insisted there is no need to panic at Manchester City despite the club's frustrating winless run extending to four games. Enzo Maresca's side were held to a 1-1 draw by Fulham at the Etihad, a result that continued the club's recent poor form in the Premier League . City lost three consecutive Premier League games before the international break, but failed to return to winning ways as Fulham earned a point. Rodrigo Muniz fired Fulham in front inside 16 minutes, after good work from former City winger Oscar Bobb down the right. Erling Haaland had a goal disallowed just nine minutes later, with City heading into the interval behind. Anderson's equaliser brought the home side level after half-time, as the summer signing drove a brilliant volley through traffic to level. Fulham had the better chances to win it with Gianluigi Donnarumma forced into second-half saves, with Anderson admitting City struggled to find another gear. “It’s very frustrating,” Anderson said to City studios at full-time . “Going a goal down wasn’t ideal but it seems to be happening. The second half was better, more intensity, we pushed higher. We just struggled to get the second goal. “We’re working on that [falling behind so much]. We are doing everything we can to fix it. “Every game we are learning things. We’ll train harder. We’ll be ready for the next one.” The draw leaves City third in the Premier League table, five points behind Arsenal, having played a game more. Despite that gap, Anderson said there's no reason to panic for a City side still 'building' under Maresca. “We’re building it. It’s a new team, new players, everything is new. We’re all learning off each other and we’re only building relationships. “It’s early days in this era. Hopefully we can get there.”

item.title: Week 11 Fantasy Football Pivot Options For Brock Bowers, Mike Evans, And Two More Injured Stars
item.description: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers (89) during the fourth quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kyle Terada-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Much like every week, there are a ton of fantasy football stars who have either been ruled out for Week 11 or are questionable and could miss this weekend's game. Fantasy owners have to be prepared and have a pivot option in case the player they are relying on gets moved, even if they end up being a surprising game-time inactive. These are the top pivot-option injury replacements for Week 11. RB Emmett Johnson, Kansas City Chiefs We all know this one, but it would be irresponsible to not mention the most important injury replacement of the week. Not only is Johnson replacing the most important injured player, but he is also the best replacement of the week. The Chiefs have already ruled out Kenneth Walker III for Week 11 , so there won't be any surprises here. Johnson should be viewed as an RB1 this week in an ideal matchup against the Arizona Cardinals after going off for 171 total yards and two touchdowns last week. WR Deebo Samuel, San Francisco 49ers Mike Evans has a chance to return this week, but he is not a lock to get back out on the field. He's a 33-year-old with an Achilles injury; they aren't putting him out there if he's not 100% during warm-ups before the game. Samuel would serve as the WR1 if Evans is unable to go. In his return from injury last week, with Evans inactive, Samuel racked up 110 total yards and two touchdowns. TE Michael Mayer, Las Vegas Raiders This is the one that everyone will be watching for. Brock Bowers is expected to be a game-time decision, and it's hard to know what to believe from the Raiders' coaching staff. What we do know is that Bowers got in two limited practices this week and is listed as questionable. If Bowers is ruled out, Mayer could be in for a huge day in a great matchup against the Denver Broncos. Denver is allowing the third-most points to fantasy tight ends this season. TE Dawson Knox, Buffalo Bills Dalton Kincaid being listed as doubtful has flown under the radar a bit this week because all the attention to tight ends has been diverted towards Bowers. Still, a lot of fantasy owners have been rolling with Kincaid, and the most frustrating part about watching him is having to deal with Knox stealing catches. Knox won't have to deal with Kincaid stealing his receptions this week. item.title: Will India and Pakistan players shake hands in Asia Cup 2026 Rising stars match? Revisiting recent history of no-handshake policy
item.description: Will India and Pakistan players shake hands in Asia Cup 2026 Rising stars match? Revisiting recent history of no-handshake policy originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: India 'A' face Pakistan Shaheens in the Asia Cup Rising Stars on Sunday in Doha. India have not shaken hands with Pakistan in any fixture since September 2025. The two sides skipped handshakes before and after this same fixture last November. Will India and Pakistan players shake hands in the Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 match? The question arrives before every India-Pakistan fixture now, and it tends to be answered before a ball is bowled. Tilak Varma's India 'A' meet Abdul Samad's Pakistan Shaheens on Sunday, November 22, at the West End Park International Cricket Stadium in Doha. The game starts at 3:30 p.m. IST, which is 1:00 p.m. local time, and it is the second of three group matches for both sides. On every precedent available, the answer is no. The BCCI's policy has held without exception since it was introduced, and nothing in the build-up to this tournament suggests it is being revisited. The two captains are expected to go through the toss without the customary greeting, as Indian and Pakistani captains have done in every format for more than a year. MORE: Sarfaraz recalls Gambhir's phone call over dressing-room leak reports after BGT 2025 How did the India-Pakistan no-handshake policy begin after the Pahalgam attack? The BCCI introduced the protocol at the 2025 Men's Asia Cup, as a direct response to the Pahalgam terror attack of April 22, 2025. Under Suryakumar Yadav's captaincy, the Indian men's team avoided handshakes with Salman Ali Agha's Pakistan side in all three meetings at that tournament, including the final. What began as a stance for one tournament has since become standard practice across Indian cricket, cutting across age groups, genders and formats. The Rising Stars tournament followed a month later, and it is the most relevant precedent for Sunday. India A skipped the handshakes both before and after the game in November 2025, a match Pakistan Shaheens won by eight wickets on their way to the title. item.title: The potential reason why Patriots’ Drake Maye, AJ Brown havent been placed on IR
item.description: Eric Canha-Imagn Images The potential reason why Patriots’ Drake Maye, AJ Brown havent been placed on IR appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New England Patriots have yet to place quarterback Drake Maye or wide receiver AJ Brown on injured reserve. The team has three regular-season return designations left and may already have plans for two of them. Both players suffered injuries November 15 in a 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich. Defensive end Aidan Hutchinson sacked Maye on the final play of New England’s opening drive. Brown injured his hamstring in the third quarter. Tests showed Maye fractured his right fibula . The injury does not require surgery, but he could miss the rest of the regular season. The Patriots expect Brown to miss multiple weeks. Teams can designate up to eight players to return during the regular season. The Patriots have used five designations, including one to bring back Brown after he suffered a high ankle sprain in the season opener. Guard Alijah Vera-Tucker and receiver Romeo Doubs are both eligible to return next week and could account for two more designations. If the Patriots use both, they would have one regular-season designation left for Maye, Brown or another injured player. item.title: Moises Caicedo forced off in tears as Chelsea injury crisis worsens
item.description: Moises Caicedo was forced off in the first half of Chelsea’s clash with Leeds as Xabi Alonso ’s injury problems continue to mount. The Ecuadorian lynchpin suffered a bad landing after meeting James Justin’s aerial challenge, which saw him twist in midair and land on his tailbone. Caicedo was initially able to continue but after being troubled by his back in the following minutes, repeatedly holding the problem area, he went down off the ball, covering his seemingly tearful eyes with his shirt in dejection. He was replaced by Jordan Henderson in the 22nd minute, but did not go straight down the tunnel for further treatment, instead taking a seat on the bench with an ice pack. The circumstances in which Caicedo’s injury was dealt with left the Chelsea dugout unhappy with referee Michael Oliver. Caicedo agonised on the deck for a considerable period before the Blues eventually sent their medical team on to treat him, with club doctors delaying their entry onto the pitch to try and prevent him having to come off for a minute, as per a new rule introduced in the Premier League this season. Seemingly for the same reason, Caicedo leapt up and refused treatment from Chelsea medics when they approached him, but Oliver still ordered him to the touchline, reducing Chelsea to 10 men for a minute. Caicedo also suffered a fitness scare during the international break when he was replaced at half-time of Ecuador’s 2-0 friendly win over Bolivia in midweek after feeling unwell.

item.title: Ex-captain Moody joins England in emotional haka response
item.description: Lewis Moody walked with current England captain Maro Itoje to join England's side to face New Zealand's haka [Getty Images] Former England captain Lewis Moody joined the current team to face New Zealand's haka in an emotional start to Saturday's Test match at Allianz Stadium. Moody, who was diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND) last year, stood at the centre of England's line-up - between captain Maro Itoje and one of the team's vice-captains, Ellis Genge - as they faced up to the traditional pre-match challenge. Led by Genge's fellow vice-captains Ollie Chessum and Jamie George, England then advanced to form a V shape, similar to the formation they took before last year's victory and the 2019 Rugby World Cup semi-final win against the All Blacks. Moody, who was embraced by most of England's team in the aftermath of the challenge and its acceptance, also delivered the match ball. Follow live coverage of England v New Zealand England stars to help launch Moody MND challenge at All Blacks match With Twickenham energised, England started the match fast, with Henry Slade getting on the end of a Fin Smith grubber kick to score the first try after just four minutes. All of England's players are wearing boots emblazoned with the logo of Moody's Front Up to MND campaign, to which signed warm-up and match-worn shirts will be donated. The campaign's first fundraising drive is a mass-participation coastal walk in June, which aims to raise more than £1m to fund research into the disease. A statement from England Rugby said: "As a hugely respected former England captain, it was important to the England men's team to show their support for Lewis and to involve him in many areas of the match day, including on the pitch. "Supporting Lewis and Front Up reflects the game's commitment to standing alongside those affected by MND, and to help raise awareness and funds for research." Moody delivered the match ball before England's victory over Australia last autumn, a few weeks after he revealed his diagnosis in an interview with BBC Breakfast. Last weekend, Wales players were bathed in red light and smoke during the All Blacks' haka in a response that was 'a year in the making' .

item.description: Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Joe Burrow is proving to be a strong candidate for the MVP award this season, with his stunning performances for the Cincinnati Bengals. How Joe Burrow reminds Michael Irvin of Troy Aikman As Aikman continues to battle behind the scenes with ESPN and Joe Buck amid his uncertain future with the network, it is easy to forget the incredible career he enjoyed as a quarterback. Two masked burglars broke into the Los Angeles home of tennis champion Sloane Stephens, apparently expecting an easy target. Instead, barking dogs, alert housesitters, and a shouted warning sent them running before they could steal a thing. The frightening encounter unfolded Tuesday night, November 17, at the 2017 U.S. Open champion's home in Sherman Oaks, California. Investigators say the intruders smashed their way inside while Stephens was away, unaware that people were staying at the property. A silent alarm alerted police, but it was the noise inside the house that gave the residents their first warning. When someone shouted about getting a gun, the suspects apparently decided the property wasn't worth the risk. The incident ended with three people in police custody following a BMW pursuit across Los Angeles. It also raised familiar concerns for homeowners: even expensive properties with security systems can be vulnerable, and sometimes the simplest warnings make the biggest difference. The suspects were described as wearing black clothing and face coverings. The intruders had reportedly used a crowbar to break through a glass door. Yet the sound of shattering glass was only the beginning of their problems. Dogs inside the home began barking, waking the people who were housesitting for Stephens. Rather than finding an empty mansion, the intruders encountered residents who knew something was wrong. One person called 911. According to law enforcement sources cited by the Los Angeles Times, someone inside shouted, "Get the gun." The warning apparently worked. The masked intruders fled without taking anything, and officers who initially searched the surrounding neighborhood were unable to locate them. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
